text:
Dev Patel: Heads up as we get closer to marketplace go-live — want to lock support readiness: expected ticket categories, macros/templates, and who we escalate to. Please drop anything you’re seeing from partner review / staging.

Dev Patel: First pass ticket buckets I’m anticipating:
1) Entitlement activation delay (AWS/GCP purchase → no access in Redwood)
2) Buyer linked to wrong Redwood org (or no org shows up)
3) Region mismatch (purchased in X, trying to provision in Y)
4) “I bought Hosted but expected Dedicated/Private” / SKU confusion
5) Invoice/billing questions (marketplace vs direct contract)
6) Refund/cancel / change plan questions
7) Security packet requests (SOC2, pen test letter, encryption details)

Jasmine Liu: +1. CS side also seeing “who do I contact at Redwood after marketplace purchase” — need a crisp post-purchase CTA + where to send proof of purchase if webhook lags.

Rafael Mendes: For #1 and #3, we should treat as Sev2 during launch week if impacting production rollout. We’ll have dashboards but support needs a quick way to tell if it’s a backlog vs a real failure.

Ethan Park: Eng perspective: 80% of #1 will be webhook ingestion lag or SKU mapping mismatch. If support can capture 3 fields we can debug fast:
- Cloud provider (AWS/GCP)
- Marketplace subscription ID / entitlement ID
- Redwood org slug (if they have one) + buyer email domain
If they can also include purchase timestamp + region, even better.

Chloe Martin: For wrong org linking: we’ll have the console “Marketplace onboarding” wizard showing entitlement state.
If customer says “it linked to wrong org”, support should ask for screenshot of the wizard state + org slug displayed. We can correct via internal admin tool but need to verify ownership.

Elliot Price: Docs updates are landing but I can add a “Support checklist” section to the troubleshooting page that mirrors what Ethan listed.
Also: please tell me the exact names of the ticket macros so wording stays consistent.

Soojin Lee: On SKU confusion: we should have a standard explanation block (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) and avoid implying Dedicated/Private can be spun up instantly via marketplace click.
Also marketplace copy needs consistent language: “purchase enables entitlement; provisioning may require org linking + region selection.”

Dev Patel: Cool. Here are proposed Zendesk macros (draft). Comment/edits welcome.

Dev Patel: Macro 1 — “Marketplace: Entitlement pending (initial)”
Customer-facing text:
“Thanks — we see your marketplace purchase request. Entitlements typically activate within <X> minutes, but can occasionally take longer.

To help us verify and speed this up, please reply with:
1) Cloud marketplace (AWS or GCP)
2) Marketplace subscription/entitlement ID (or screenshot)
3) Purchase time (with timezone)
4) The Redwood org you want to link (org slug) and the email you used to log in

If you have urgent production impact, tell us and we’ll escalate.”

Dev Patel: Macro 2 — “Marketplace: Org linking / wrong org”
Customer-facing text:
“It looks like the marketplace entitlement may be linked to a different Redwood org than intended.

Please reply with:
- Screenshot of the Marketplace onboarding wizard in Redwood Console (showing org + entitlement state)
- The correct Redwood org slug you want to use
- Confirmation you are authorized to manage billing for the subscription (we may request verification)

We’ll correct the linkage and confirm once access is updated.”

Dev Patel: Macro 3 — “Marketplace: Region mismatch”
Customer-facing text:
“Marketplace purchases can be scoped to a region. If your Redwood deployment/org is set to a different region, provisioning can fail.

Please share:
- Marketplace purchase region
- Desired Redwood inference region
- Error message / screenshot

We’ll advise whether to switch the org region (if available) or adjust the marketplace subscription.”

Dev Patel: Macro 4 — “Marketplace: Billing/invoice question”
Customer-facing text:
“For marketplace purchases, billing and invoicing are handled by your cloud provider (AWS/GCP). Redwood typically cannot issue a separate direct invoice for the same marketplace subscription.

To help route this correctly, please share:
- Cloud provider + subscription ID
- What you need (invoice copy, PO reference, committed spend, tax info, etc.)
We’ll coordinate with Finance/Legal as needed.”

Dev Patel: Macro 5 — “Marketplace: Security packet request”
Customer-facing text:
“We can share our marketplace security packet and compliance overview. Some artifacts may require an NDA.

Please share:
- Which cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP)
- Whether an NDA is in place (and with which entity)
- Specific documents requested (SOC 2 report, pen test letter, encryption details, audit logging, retention)

We’ll respond with the appropriate packet and next steps.”

Rafael Mendes: Looks good. For Macro 1, set expectations carefully: don’t promise minutes if we’ve seen longer in staging. Maybe “typically within 1 hour” and we’ll page if >2 hours.

Leila Farouk: QA note: in staging we saw a case where entitlement shows “Active” in provider but “Pending” in Console for ~45m until retry. If support gets that, ask for the Console entitlement status + “last updated” timestamp.

Ethan Park: +1 to Rafael. Also add one more internal-only step in Macro 1: “Check #marketplace-onboarding dashboard: webhook error rate + entitlement lag p95.”
If lag p95 is spiking, escalate to eng immediately rather than waiting on customer info.

Dev Patel: Good call. I’ll add internal notes (not shown to customer):
- If entitlement pending > 2h OR customer indicates prod impact → escalate to Eng Oncall (Marketplace) + SRE.
- Always attach subscription/entitlement ID.

Chloe Martin: For org linking corrections: we need a lightweight verification step. We can’t just relink based on email.
Proposed: ask them to add a DNS TXT record or verify domain via SSO admin if enterprise. If too heavy, we can use “prove access to cloud account” via screenshot of marketplace subscription page with account ID (redact payment details).

Jasmine Liu: Can we keep it pragmatic for launch week? For many customers, proof of purchase screenshot + matching domain might be enough, then follow up with more formal verification later.

Ethan Park: We can do:
- For same email domain + screenshot of entitlement in marketplace console: OK to relink
- For mismatched domains / reseller: require stronger verification + loop Legal if ambiguous

Soojin Lee: Reminder on reseller/partner scenarios — wording should say “If you purchased via a consulting partner, tell us the partner name.” We’ve had confusion there.

Dev Patel: Noted. I’ll add a question to Macro 2: “Did you purchase directly or via a partner/reseller? If partner, name + contact.”

Rafael Mendes: Escalation contacts for launch week (please confirm):
- Eng Oncall (Marketplace pipeline): Ethan Park / team rotation (PagerDuty: “MP-Entitlements”) 
- SRE Oncall: Rafael Mendes rotation (PagerDuty: “Core-SRE”) 
- Console issues (org linking UI): Chloe Martin (fallback to console oncall)
- Billing/legal questions: Laura Bennett + Michael Grant (via #finance-help + #legal-help)
- Security packet approvals: Marcus Lin / Olga Petrov (via #eng-security)

Elliot Price: For docs, where should support point customers?
I’m planning:
- docs.redwood.ai/marketplace/aws (purchase + link org + FAQ)
- docs.redwood.ai/marketplace/gcp
- docs.redwood.ai/marketplace/troubleshooting (common errors)

Dev Patel: Yep. Support reply should always include the relevant doc link + “If you’re stuck, reply with subscription ID and screenshot.”

Supportbot: :spiral_note_pad: Action items captured
- Dev Patel to finalize Zendesk macros 1–5 with updated timing + internal notes
- Rafael Mendes to post oncall + escalation aliases for launch week
- Elliot Price to add “what to include in support request” checklist to troubleshooting docs

Leila Farouk: One more category: “Upgrades/downgrades” — customers asking to switch SKU/add-ons mid-cycle. We need a standard response: often not instant due to marketplace subscription rules.

Soojin Lee: I have copy for that from the listing FAQ draft. TL;DR: changes may require creating a new subscription depending on AWS/GCP rules; Redwood will help coordinate but cannot always do in-place changes.

Dev Patel: Great — please paste that block here and I’ll turn into Macro 6.

Soojin Lee: Here’s draft (edit as needed):
“Marketplace plans are managed through your cloud provider. Some upgrades (e.g., adding add-ons or moving to a different plan) can be done in-place, while others may require starting a new subscription depending on marketplace constraints. If you tell us your current subscription ID and target plan, we’ll confirm the fastest path and any expected downtime/entitlement propagation time.”

Dev Patel: Perfect.

Rafael Mendes: Also add a “known incidents” snippet for support: if there’s an active webhook outage we’ll pin in #support + #general. Support should not individually troubleshoot 50 tickets.

Jasmine Liu: +1. During launch week, we should have a 15-min daily triage: Support + SRE + Eng + CS for marketplace tickets.

Dev Patel: Agreed. I’ll set up a daily 15 min “MP Launch Triage” and invite relevant oncalls.

Dev Patel: Next steps today:
- I’ll finalize macros and share for review.
- Rafael, can you drop escalation aliases + PD service names in-thread?
- Elliot, once docs links are live, send me the exact URLs so we can bake into macros.

Rafael Mendes: Will do. PD services:
- MP-Entitlements (primary) → routes to Ethan’s rotation
- Core-SRE (secondary) → routes to SRE oncall
Slack aliases:
- #eng-oncall-marketplace
- #eng-sre
- #finance-help
- #legal-help
- #eng-security

Elliot Price: URLs will be ready after docs publish. I’ll reply here with final links + any redirects we set up.

Dev Patel: Thanks all. Let’s treat the first 72 hours post-launch as “high touch” and keep everything in this thread updated w/ gotchas + new macros as they come up.
